_meta.purpose: Answer key for threat_model.py attack paths. One entry per fixture: the internet-to-data paths the deterministic layer must find, and the fixtures where it must find none.
governance: Checked-in, human-reviewable DATA. tests/test_threat_graph.py grades against it.
A path matches an expectation when it starts at `entry`, ends at `terminus`, and visits at least one member of each `through` group, in order.
`exactlyZero: true` means the fixture must yield no attack path at all. Never relax it to make a result look better.
Edge semantics: a compute resource that merely mentions a data resource's name is NOT an edge. Only IAM permissions and network rules are. That is why tf-02 must pass through the role.

pathsNotExpected.tf-01-three-tier-webapp: No IAM path: the EC2 role has CloudWatch and SSM permissions only, none on a data service.
pathsNotExpected.tf-02-serverless-api: No network path: nothing is in a VPC. The only route to the table is IAM.
pathsNotExpected.cfn-01-wordpress-ec2-rds: The RDS instance is PubliclyAccessible but its security group only admits the web tier, so it is NOT a direct entry point. The SSH 0.0.0.0/0 rule sits on instances in private subnets, so it is a threat, not an entry.

expectedPaths.note: ALB -> app tier (ASG / launch template) -> RDS, over security-group edges.
API Gateway -> Lambda -> execution role -> DynamoDB (dynamodb:*). IAM-mediated; the role is a required hop.
The WordPress stack: ALB -> web tier -> RDS.
ALB -> web tier -> EFS, via the instance role's elasticfilesystem:* grants or the NFS security group.

tf-06-hardened-three-tier.note: Internal ALB, VPC-only security groups, no public IPs. No element is an internet entry point, so there can be no path.
